stem: The preoperative nurse reviews four adult clients who will receive general anesthesia. Which client has the greatest recognized risk for postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV)?

options.A: A male client who smokes, has no prior PONV or motion sickness, and is expected to avoid postoperative opioids
options.B: A female client who does not smoke, has a history of motion sickness, and is expected to require postoperative opioids
options.C: A male client who does not smoke, has no prior PONV, and is expected to receive nonopioid postoperative analgesia
options.D: A female client who smokes, has no history of PONV or motion sickness, and is expected to avoid postoperative opioids

rationale: Established adult PONV risk factors include female sex, nonsmoking status, previous PONV or motion sickness, and opioid exposure. Client B has all four of these commonly used predictors, whereas each other option has fewer recognized factors. Risk assessment helps the perioperative team individualize prophylaxis; the item does not assign a universal drug regimen or numeric probability from the risk profile alone.
educational_objective: Recognize major adult PONV risk factors during preoperative assessment so clients at higher risk can be identified for individualized prevention planning.
source_document_title: Fifth Consensus Guidelines for the Management of Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting: Executive Summary; Clinical practice guidelines for the prevention and management of postoperative nausea and vomiting (2025 edition)
source_locator: PONV Risk Assessment / established adult risk factors; simplified Apfel predictors: female sex, history of PONV or motion sickness, nonsmoking status, postoperative opioid use
source_claim_supported: Current 2025 PONV guidelines identify female sex, nonsmoking, prior PONV/motion sickness, and opioid exposure as established adult risk factors used for risk stratification.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — provide preoperative care; assess risk factors and recognize potential complications associated with procedures/treatments
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative complication-risk assessment
correction_summary: Retained the evidence-supported PONV risk construct but converted the recall list into comparative preoperative risk assessment, corrected the blueprint from Physiological Adaptation to Reduction of Risk Potential, and removed vague/absurd distractors.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: 2025 Fifth Consensus executive summary and 2025 evidence-based guideline reviewed; risk-factor set is current and concordant.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Female sex, nonsmoking, prior PONV/motion sickness and opioid exposure are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; contains all four established predictors used in common adult risk stratification.
audit_findings.choice_C: Contains nonsmoking only among the four emphasized predictors.
audit_findings.choice_D: Contains female sex but smoking/no history/no opioid lower the compared risk profile.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: B uniquely contains the complete risk-factor cluster; no numeric incidence or universal prophylaxis threshold is asserted.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are parallel client profiles with comparable structure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Reduction of Risk Potential is the stronger NCSBN fit for preoperative risk recognition.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked age, anesthetic type and surgical-procedure confounders; all clients are stated to receive general anesthesia and no surgery-specific differences are introduced, preserving a single best comparison.
